programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Cyclone Separator Shootout
programme.desc: A cyclone separator is essentially a bucket with a fancy lid. When connected to a vacuum source, the lid creates a cyclonic suction that collects large dust particles minimally and the small dust particles at best. By adding one of these to a standard shop vac or dust extractor, you can collect much of the dust before it ever reaches your vac's filter.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Shop Update - End of Phase 1
programme.desc: I'm officially done with Phase 1 of the garage to shop conversion and I'm ready to start building. I wanted to bring you up to speed by showing the various changes I've made up to this point for those who've been following along with my progress. None of these things warranted a standalone video so I figured I'd lump them all into one recap.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: A Miter Gauge that Does One Angle?!
programme.desc: Woodpeckers new Exact-90 Miter Gauge only cuts one angle and costs a bundle, but there's more than meets the eye here.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Router-Based Inlay
programme.desc: Inlay is a great way to adorn your woodworking projects. Even the simplest item can become incredibly compelling if it features a well-executed inlay. With the right materials and techniques, its just like painting with wood. Only “non-artistic” folks like myself can actually do it!

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: This Spatula Cost Me $33 000!
programme.desc: Making your own spatula is super easy with $33k worth of tools!

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Gadget Station Part 12
programme.desc: Well I finally made it to the finish line. This episode covers the hinge installation, pegging the tenons in the doors, making custom ebony handles, and finishing. I end the video with a justification of my design.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Sanding Efficiency
programme.desc: Sanding is one of those tasks that nobody enjoys. So in order to get the best results with the least amount of effort, we need to consider the things that have the most dramatic effect on our sanding efficiency.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Be a Safety Hero!
programme.desc: Last week I asked you folks for your favorite quick safety tips and you were kind enough to respond with some fun and insightful tricks of the trade. So I took a few of my favorites and bundled them up in this 50's style educational video. I hope you enjoy!

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Gadget Station Part 3
programme.desc: This episode is primarily focused on the design of the legs. I present several options and show how I create a basic template. At the end, you will see the final test leg. The process of cutting the leg itself will be covered in detail when we cut the final legs out of the bubinga stock.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Duluth Wine Box
programme.desc: Learn to create a stylish Japanese-inspired wine box with this step-by-step tutorial. Ideal as a holiday gift, this elegant wooden box is modeled after a traditional Japanese toolbox. Follow along as we guide you through the woodworking process, from selecting materials to assembling the final product. Sponsored by Duluth Trading Company, this video combines craftsmanship with a touch of humor, ensuring both an informative and entertaining experience.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Nesting Tables

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: The Effects of Weather on Untreated Wood
programme.desc: Mother Nature can be quite harsh on wood even under the best conditions. This is why it is essential to protect your outdoor projects with a good quality finish and if possible, use a cover to protect them from the elements.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: How to Create Pillowed Legs
programme.desc: Whenever I make legs for a table or chair, I find it difficult to leave them square and flat on each face. Ever since I saw David Marks pillow the outside faces of his Bubinga Coffee Table on WoodWorks, I always like to consider the possibility of using that technique to spice things up.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Gadget Station Part 5
programme.desc: Road Trip! I was originally convinced that the Gadget Station would call for knife hinges. programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Classy Headphone Controller Rack

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Mid-Century Modern Dining Table
programme.desc: I sat down to design a new dining table for my brother-in-law Jason and before I was done I realized it was totally inspired by my time with Jory Brigham. The table has splayed legs, a large overhanging top, and bevels and tapers galore.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Wall Hanging Tool Chest Part 2
programme.desc: With the design mostly complete, we can start the construction phase. My goal is to build the project entirely out of Baltic Birch plywood. Its cheap, stable, and doesn't look half bad even without edge treatments! It really is the perfect material for shop furniture and jigs.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Sculpted End Table Part 2

programme.desc: Recently, my son has been obsessed with the Disney movie Moana. One of the primary characters is the demigod Maui who wields a magical hook. The hook has a very distinct look and is adorned with special carvings. Using a single 2×4, I made a kid-sized version of the hook.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Why Did My Cutting Board Split?
programme.desc: I don't know if this ever happens to you, but sometimes my tools just get out of whack and start to sound funny. Take a listen and let me know if you have any advice. Also have you ever wondered why end grain cutting boards are prone to splitting? Here's a couple of reasons why!

programme.desc: I assemble and attach the base, install the handles, and apply the final finish to the top. This project was an incredible learning experience, and not in the way you might think. I have a new found appreciation for the tools I have been taking granted for years.
